Management: 
Good afternoon, and thank you all for joining Knack Packaging Q2 and Half-Year 1 Financial 
Year 2027 earnings call. On the call, I am joined by Dr. Ajay Kumar Dubey, our Chief Financial 
Officer, and Adfactor PR, our Investor Relations partners. 
I'm pleased to share that Quarter 2 FY27 was a stable and strong growth for Knack Packaging. 
In Quarter 2 FY27, we delivered our highest ever quarterly revenue. On a consolidated basis, 
the revenue from operations rose 52.5%, EBITDA rose 29.9%, and PAT rose 21.2%, all on year-
on-year basis. 
Talking about the industry, the first half of the year was a challenging period from an input cost 
perspective. The conflict in West Asia disrupted supplies and price of polypropylene. Our key 
raw material rose more than 50% within few weeks, and the prices remain elevated throughout 
the quarter. 
At the same time, disruption in the Red Sea increased the freight cost, which matters to us as an 
exporter to 75 countries. This factor exerted pressure on the industry as an increase in input and 
logistic costs outpaced the pace of corresponding selling price revision. 
Knack was impacted by this industry-wide cost pressure. However, with our 3 decades of 
experience, long-standing relationship with our vendor, and strong procurement ecosystem, we 
were able to mitigate the price rise. 
Talking about our EBITDA, it grew on absolute basis. However, the EBITDA margin was 
impacted in Q2 FY27. About 45% to 50% of our customers are on conversion cost model where 
the bag price moves with the polymer price.

But this price revision takes effect and we have already revised prices with our customer and 
initiated cost pass-through. And we expect this to reflect in our realization from Quarter 3 FY27 
onwards, subject to market conditions stabilization. 
Despite this, we see immense growth in the industry. Our growth ahead lies in our competitive 
strength We have focused on 3 key pillars, which are product innovation, integrated 
manufacturing facility, and our long-term customer relationship. 
We work closely with major companies in food, pet nutrition, fertilizer, and other 25 plus 
industries, and many of our customers have grown with us. Packaging typically accounts for 
only about 1% to 2% of our customers' end product price, yet it is often the first physical touch 
point between a brand and its consumer and can influence the purchase decision, especially in 
the competitive categories. 
Once supplier has proven its reliability and consistency, customer rarely risks a change. As a 
result, our customer stickiness is very high. As on 30 September 2026, we served more than 
2,040 customers with 13,974 SKUs, up from 2,000 customers and 13,500 SKUs at the end of 
Quarter 1 Financial Year 2027. 
Our export market contributed a significant part of our revenue during the half as of September 
2026, and we sold to 75 countries across 6 continents, up from 74 countries at the end of Quarter 
1 FY27 and 71 countries in FY26. 
Our exports included US, Europe, Asia, and Africa. Coming to H1 FY27, our top-line growth 
was driven by significantly higher export volumes, deeper wallet share with existing global 
FMCG, pet food, and agri customers and addition of new international accounts. 
We saw sustained demand from our premium bags both domestically and in our export market. 
Importantly, we began fulfilling orders from new customers ahead of our next phase of capacity 
expansion. 
As a recent update, on 2nd October 2026, we announced a new order and 3-year contract renewal 
worth about INR150 crores per year from an international customer, one of the largest private 
corporations in the world from the pet food and animal nutrition packaging, including in the 
United States. This renewal underscores our reliability and our product quality at a global scale. 
Looking ahead to the rest of FY27, our focus will be on profitable growth. Our priority is to 
restore our EBITDA margin as pricing adjustments flow through from Quarter 3 FY27 and then 
to improve it further by increasing the share of value-added products, controlling costs, 
leveraging our integrated setup. We also scaling up the Sayem Knack JV in Mexico towards 
breakeven and building our order book more stronger. 
Now I will hand over to Dr. Ajay Kumar Dubey, our CFO, who will provide the detailed 
financial highlights for Q2 and H1 FY27.
